name: School of Chiron

prefs.cog: Stay at the room's mechanism for

tithe.hint: Obols today: tokens and working time

prefs.questions: A question at the end of a turn counts as an aporia
prefs.pauseHint: Near-zero CPU when unseen; aporiai still alert.

watch.name: Argos
watch.button: Night Vigil: Argos shuts the PC down once every session waits on you

notes: Pelion, the school of Chiron, not 40k: a marble stoa on Mount Pelion open onto the Aegean, where the centaur Chiron teaches; sessions are his students. No gods, no togas, no ruins: new marble painted with a blue and a red band, oil lamps at night, one machine only (the mechanism).
art: the families listed in art are Pelion's own (see the art lines below); later tasks redraw the rest in the slots below.

px: marble wall plates a shadowed grey-blue (4 5, lit edges 7 8, joints 6, flute shade 9), a step darker and cooler than the linen so a student reads against them; the plinth 0, wall tops A; pebble-mosaic floor in bluish white (1, lit top 3, shaded foot the marble's 8, gaps 2); the sanctum's walls painted red (D E, H K) over its rosette floor on an Aegean blue field (u)
px: bronze for every metal: brass slots (g G h U) bright bronze, the iron slot m darker bronze with a green patina shadow (M V) (its sheen l is now the coat, below)

px l T: Chiron's chestnut coat, lit and mid (Z, the tablets' wax, its shade; j z its dark tail, with w strands): retuned from the iron sheen and the rank seam, slots no drawn Pelion family used; base art not yet redrawn that draws in them (the 39° figures) shows them chestnut until it is
px: undyed linen for the student's chiton (b B) and, a shade deeper, his himation (r R d, the border t in the cloth); the wreath z j in the hair's colours; the helper's tunic (q Q) a darker sand
px: olive wood (w W L), papyrus (p P), Aegean blue (u), olive green (v), brick red (x) for the painted bands; Y the olive leaf's silver underside
px: amber (c C o O) for the tablets' writing and the owl's eyes, lamplight flames (f F); the mechanism's dials polished bronze (h g, the inner faces m)

px: the floor channels (! +) a meander, dark on white pebbles; the void beyond the gate (@ $ %) the mountain path at dusk; the beacon (& * - =) a bronze torch, = * - also the terracotta of the pottery and sherds (lit by ), the coverlet's red); the seals (( ) [) red clay; $ % also the wine and the grapes
sash: painted Greek pigments, none the high rank's gold
rank.high: a deep blue himation, gold border and wreath; standard: undyed linen, nothing shows; novice: grey cloth throughout. The helpers by the same rule on their tunic and satchel
ink: the texture inks faint on marble (no binary cant, light grime, scratches a faint cool grey); screenOff the dimmed writing on an unlit table

ink (the mechanism): the app's moving marks on its dials are engraving, not light: phosphor, screenDim and screenMark dark and mid bronze, screenHot a bright glint on a pointer, screenFlicker a faint sheen passing over the bronze; lampDead a dark bronze over the seven wanderers' beads not lit. phosphor also tints the pulse running down a suzerain's cord
ink.alarm, light.skullAlarm: the owl's eyes and its glow over a stale aporia, a warm amber, not red (alarm also tints the burn's last embers)

ink.windowDay: the view between two columns, only these slots drawn in it: u sky, o the haze over the horizon, v sea, Z deep sea, g the sun's glitter (by night the moon's path), x the island, a the sun (sky by night), h the stars and the crescent moon (sky by day)
light: lamplight amber, a blue-grey night

ui: a dark chrome in the stone's blue-grey with bronze and Aegean accents, papyrus cards, terminal type; --honours-ink a pale gilt, the words written on the stele's dark bronze tablets (the night darkens the art, never the words, so no ink reads on bare marble both by day and by night)
text: Greek words in Latin transliteration, macrons kept (Mathētēs, Ephēbos); a petition is an aporia, the watchman Argos
text.inRooms: the rooms plan's words

art scribe: the students: bare-headed under an olive wreath (z j), a linen chiton to the knee (b B), a himation over the left shoulder and across the body (r R d), swag folds under its band and an uneven hem with one border (t), the department band (y, a dark seam under it) across the chest, the back and the side; the near arm bent at the elbow in the side view; sandals; the arm frame the forearm at rest, bent forward from the elbow toward the belt (at the table: the hands on it; standing: the hands folded), no stylus (anchors arm, armL moved). px and rank.novice.robe give z j the hair's colours so the wreath shows only in gold; novice's chiton b B grey

art adept: the helpers: a smaller boy in a short tunic (q Q, lit b) with a trimmed neckline and hem (J I), a leather satchel on a strap across the body whose flap is the kind glyph, front and back (an eye, a written tablet, a rosette, a meander), his arms down along the body, a papyrus roll held across his chest, sandals; from the side the satchel a soft bag on the hip; rank.high.adept.b is the tunic's lit blue

art room-walls: the stoa's back wall: dressed marble courses (24 x 10 blocks set over by half, lit top and draft, faint light veins) under a painted Doric frieze (cornice, blue triglyphs between plain metopes, a red taenia, blue guttae, architrave); the wall foot a two-step plinth; the sanctum the same frieze over courses painted red; pillars fluted shafts; the bays' pilasters Doric (abacus, echinus, fluted drums); the beacon a bronze torch in a wall bracket, its pitch dark or its flame lit (anchors centre and sweep moved to the bracket and the flame)

art room-floor: a quiet mosaic of bluish white pebbles, 3 x 3 in courses set over by half, lit along the top and shaded along the bottom, its two variants a course shifted by a pebble; the channels a meander band (a Greek key, dark on white pebbles, no glow); sills and the passage marble thresholds; the sanctum's floor a rosette mosaic on Aegean blue: corner squares framed in a dark rule with a white rosette, a meander border between dark rules, a field of small white flowers

art room-doors: bronze double doors seen from above between marble jamb blocks: studded leaves with a cross rail and ring pulls at the meeting edge, the sanctum's a taller pair; half the leaves swung, in shade, over the marble threshold; open the leaves edge on against the jambs

art room-pipes: an olive garland in place of the pipes (dark and silver-green leaves on a twisted rope), its hooks bronze nails with a knot of red ribbon, the wide fitting a studded bronze band round a pillar
px (workstations, walls): X the marble's lit arris (was copper, unused), s the marble face (was tan), the grey-blue shades 4 9 6; Z (unchanged) the tablets' brown wax

art workstations: the student's table a marble slab (a painted bead band on its edge) on two pedestals with a blue band, a wax diptych standing open at its back (the writing in c, lit while the student works), a bronze stylus, a pebble abacus, a clay oil lamp at the right (its flame f F, out when unlit); the reading stand an olive-wood table with a slanted board holding an open papyrus scroll, a lamp beside it, a rolled scroll on the stretcher; the helper's table a small marble top with the students' bead band on one of their pedestals, a little wax tablet propped on it; SHELL_COG a bronze armillary hoop turning on its pin, its stud marking the turn (anchors moved: screen and slate on the wax, candle on the lamp's flame, lamp over the tablet, seals on the front edge, cog at the back left)

art walls: the windows the view between two Doric marble columns under a beam with a red band, onto sky, an island and the Aegean, an olive sprig in front; the scroll racks olive-wood pigeonholes with scroll ends (some tagged), amphorae, a hydria and a krater on top (SHELF_B the same rack, scrolls in bundles); the hangings woven on a bronze rod with a fringe, HANGING red with meander bands, a wave band and a palmette, HANGING_B blue with red wave bands, a rosette and a meander, BANNER the short red one; GAUGE a small bronze vertical sundial; CENSER a bronze oil lamp on three chains

art cogitator: the Antikythera mechanism in an olive-wood case on a marble plinth: a bronze front plate with the great dial (zodiac and calendar rings, the sun's pointer with its gilt sun, the moon's with its half-silvered ball) under screen, a small dial under wave, the calendar scale (seven peg slots) under bars, four subsidiary dials, a rail of seven coloured beads for the wanderers under lamps, a plaque engraved with the instructions; the left side open on the gear train (great wheels under the left drums, pinions), the right side a plain panel with the crank's hand wheel and a winding key (the right drums); turned posts with bronze rings; on top the moon-phase ball in its ring and two bronze incense burners whose smoke is the steam from vents (anchors the default's)

art skull: Athena's little owl hovering towards us: flat round head, white brows and a pale X between big yellow eyes (o, O glint: the app's alarm inks), the beak, broad spotted wings spread, a streaked breast, talons where the seal hangs
art skull39: the owl seen from above in the 2.5D view: spotted crown and wing backs, the face foreshortened, the barred tail (anchors the default's)

art gate: a small propylon: a low pediment painted blue with a bronze rosette and corner palmettes, a Doric entablature (blue triglyphs, red discs on the metopes, red taenia), two fluted columns before the door's piers, a stepped stylobate; the leaves bronze doors with studded panels, a cross rail and ring pulls; GATE_VOID the mountain path at dusk (night violet to the sunset's glow, dark ridges, a green slope, the sand path, an olive tree)

art fire: BRAZIER a bronze tripod brazier (a lebes on three legs gathered by a ring, lion's-paw feet), its flame frames tongues leaning left then right; CANDLES three clay oil lamps on a marble block (two terracotta, one black-glazed on a bronze stand), flames at their nozzles, their frames flaring them in turn

art magos: Chiron the centaur at rest on folded legs, side on and facing left, the man turned three-quarters to us: grey-brown hair and long grey beard, a laurel wreath, bare-chested, a bronze pendant (the app's chest light, anchor chest moved to it), the himation undyed linen with a blue border over his left shoulder and across the chest, his left hand on a scroll on his back; the chestnut horse body in three masses (shoulder, barrel, round high haunch), the dark tail falling onto the fleece, the near foreleg folded with its knee forward, the near hind leg folded with the hock behind; arm his right forearm round a tall olive-wood staff planted on the floor, the app's 1 px swing a slow lean of the staff; claw his left forefinger raised over the scroll, shown now and then: a tap (anchors arm, chest, eyeL, eyeR, claw moved)

art sanctum: THRONE a lumpy grey boulder (the mouth of his cave, moss in its dip) behind a low rock ledge under a fleece whose locks hang over its face; LORD_DESK a low marble table with a blue and red painted edge on two supports, a lyre (tortoise-shell sound box, horns, bronze yoke, strings), a bronze mortar of herbs with its pestle (where the app lights the table) and scrolls, one half open; COG_MECH a bronze medallion hung high on the wall behind him (a polished rim, a laurel wreath in relief, the centaur in profile walking, his arm raised, on a dark patinated field; it does not turn); SEAL a red clay bulla stamped with a ring on a twisted cord, its ends hanging

art clutter: PAPER_STACK stacked wax tablets (olive-wood frames, the top one's dark wax written, a red cord round the upper bundle); SCROLL_PILE a round-bellied wicker basket with three papyrus rolls heaped in it; BOOKS rolls stacked like logs and tied twice with red cord (no codices); LOOSE_A, LOOSE_B loose papyrus sheets written in brown ink, one curling, one half rolled; CRATE an olive-wood chest with bronze corners and hasp heaped with ostraka (terracotta and black-glazed sherds), a black-figure transport amphora standing by it. All within the default's face volumes (the basket's rim narrower than its belly, the amphora's mouth below the heap's rows)

art petitions: SCROLL an ostrakon, a flat potsherd whose pale inner face (: +, the fired break = *) is written in four short lines; QSCROLL the same sherd cut from a black-glazed pot (n A), one large question mark scratched through to the pale clay (+): dark where a request is pale, so a question never reads as one; SCROLL_HELD a school wax tablet with a grip at its top held up by its lower corners in two hands (one leaf, never a codex)

art commits: COMMIT_TAG the clay seal's cord (x () hanging ready, a lump of raw clay (: N) on its knot where the app drops its red clay; COMMIT_STAMP a bronze seal-stamp (ring handle, waisted stem, flared foot); COMMIT_SEAL the sealed work as it stays on the table's edge: a red clay bulla stamped with a ring, a laurel sprig (v Y on a W stem) bound under it. light.stamp kept: its red-orange flash suits red clay

art refectorium: the symposion. RECAFF a red-figure bell krater (black glaze n A S, a reserved tongue band, two youths and a palmette in clay = ), a meander band, the wine $ % in its mouth) on a fluted marble pedestal, a bronze ladle hooked over its rim, a black wine jug and a clay hydria on the floor; TABLE a long low olive-wood table set with black-glazed kylikes (one before each sleeper), loaves scored with a cross, grapes, figs and a bowl of olives, its front edge and the shadow under it whole (the face sheet's board and legs); BENCH a kline: a linen mattress (b B) under a red border woven with blue, an olive-wood rail, the headrest at its left end, three red bolsters, turned legs with bronze caps (row 0 and the legs whole, as the face sheet wants); DOZE_Z a capital zeta, the Greek letter of the Z's shape, so the sign every viewer reads as sleep is written in Greek (pale X, shaded p, a hooked serif)

art breakout: the Palaistra: raked sand (P, grains p Q 3); the kerb low marble blocks (rows 0..2 of the rail clear), lit X, joints 6; posts small marble stelae with a palmette head and a red painted band; the gate a herm (a square marble pillar with a bearded head, arm tenons, a plinth) beside an olive-wood paling gate on bronze hinges and a slim marble jamb, open the leaf swung flat against the jamb over a marble sill; from above the paling's rail, bronze-capped; swung open the whole paling leaf

art enclave: a small walled garden court: grass (v, silver Y, shade M) strewn with flowers in the rule's colour (y, dyed); the balustrade a lit coping over a fascia in the rule's colour, balusters, a plinth; posts small Doric columns with a necking in the rule's colour (also the sanctum's rail in the rooms plan, untinted: the red band); the gate two small columns under a lintel painted in the rule's colour, a ribbon of it tied across, untied it hangs from the far column

art honours: the Laurels of the week cut on a marble stele: a low pediment (the tympanum blue with a painted palmette, small acroteria at its corners), the title's frieze, a moulding (a red band over dentils), the shaft widening toward its foot with four dark bronze tablets set in it (the title on one too) where the words are written in gilt, a stepped plinth; signs painted on the stone: a laurel wreath (works sealed), a clay oil lamp (the longest study), a running hare (aporiai within the minute), a black-figure prize amphora (the busiest day). Text anchors the kit's

art lift: the mēchanē, the theatre's crane: olive-wood uprights lashed with rope, its head the great beam with a wooden pulley on a bronze axle, its pit a marble footing; the cable a twisted rope; the car a wicker basket (a twill of q Q) hung from a bronze hook by four ropes, its front a wicker flap that tips out (half) and drops (open); the floor slab a marble cornice (a red band over dentils) ending on a console; the call lamp a small oil torch, its flame lit

art watch, watch39: Argos, a hoplite on his rounds: a bronze Corinthian helmet (a rounded bowl, the dark T of its face opening: eye slits either side of the nose guard, the slot between the cheek pieces with his beard in it) under a red horsehair crest (from the front a tall narrow plume, from the side a long arc from the brow to the nape), a linen corselet with a blue band and pteruges, a short red cloak, bare arms, bronze greaves, sandals; his round bronze shield on his back with an eye painted on it (whole from behind, a lens at his back from the side, its rim behind his neck from the front); a spear in the frame-left hand (upright behind him from the side); a bronze lantern with horn panes hanging at knee height from the frame-right hand, the arm down along the body (light anchor its panes, every frame); ring: the spear set down, a bronze hand bell (the kōdōn) raised. The 39° frames: S and N the front and the back, E the profile facing right, W its mirror, each with the walk

art suzerain: the mentor's exedra, a low marble platform with a shallowly curved marble bench round its north end (its back lit, the seat, the seat's front in shade, scrolled arms), paved inside with large slabs, its riser painted with a red and blue band; the link a red cord of two twisted strands; its end a red knot under a bronze cap
